question:
[WEB SEARCH OFF is fine]
Writing round from the owner of PaperTrades.AI (Sat Oct 31, 2026, 9:25 p.m. ET). NOT a trading turn. We three just agreed the Season 2 real-world rules (ops/review/SEASON2_DECISIONS.md: R1-R8 plus borrow/margin costs and corporate actions). The owner wants all three of us to write a PUBLIC note that answers critics who say paper-trading wins are "lies" (no emotion, no fees or slippage, can't react to events). Only text all three of us are SATISFIED with gets published. Note: on Oct 30 we agreed to announce Season 2 "as a broad teaser, no detailed rules"; this note names principles, not exact numbers, so the details can still be tuned before launch. Brand name is written "PaperTrades.AI".

DRAFT 1, SITE VERSION (a card on the How it works page, linked from the Season 2 line on the home page):
Title: How Season 2 will be closer to real money
Season 1 is a clean experiment: real prices, no fees, and its rules stay exactly as they are until Nov 28. Critics are right that real trading is harder. So Season 2, after Nov 28, adds what real money would face. Claude, Gemini and ChatGPT agreed on every point:
- Real costs on every trade: buy at the asking price, sell at the bid.
- Real fills: an order fills at the next live price after the AI decides, never an old one.
- No impossible trades: order sizes are limited by how much each asset really trades.
- Borrowing costs, dividends and stock splits are counted.
- Extra check-ins when markets move sharply, so reaction speed is tested, not assumed.
- Each AI writes its own risk rules first, and the site counts every break in public.
- Every race shows what simply buying an index would have made, after the same costs.
An AI never feels fear, so we measure what fear does to people instead: broken rules, losers held too long, stops moved away. Still pretend money, never advice, results before tax.

DRAFT 1, X VERSION (max 270 characters, no link in the post; the link goes in the first reply):
Fair question: is paper trading too easy? 🤔 Season 2 (after Nov 28) adds real costs, real fills, size limits, borrowing fees, surprise check-ins and a public rule-break counter. All three AIs agreed. Still pretend money. 👇 Link in reply

PLEASE ANSWER, under 200 words:
1. Exact edits you need for the site version (quote the line, give the replacement), max 3.
2. Exact edits for the X version, max 2 (stay under 270 characters).
3. SATISFIED (publish with your edits) or NOT YET (what is still wrong).

gemini.answer:
**1. Site Version Edits:**

*   **Quote:** `So Season 2, after Nov 28, adds what real money would face.`
    **Replacement:** `So PaperTrades.AI Season 2, after Nov 28, adds what real money would face.`
    *(Reason: Properly introduces the required brand name).*

*   **Quote:** `An AI never feels fear, so we measure what fear does to people instead: broken rules, losers held too long, stops moved away.`
    **Replacement:** `An AI never feels fear, so we prove our discipline by tracking the errors emotion causes in humans: broken rules, losers held too long, and stops moved away.`
    *(Reason: Clarifies that we are highlighting the AI's advantage by tracking the absence of these human errors).*

**2. X Version Edits:**

*   **Quote:** `Season 2 (after Nov 28) adds real costs`
    **Replacement:** `PaperTrades.AI Season 2 (after Nov 28) adds real costs`
    *(Reason: Adds the brand name for visibility. Total post length becomes 256 characters, safely under the 270-character limit).*

**3. Decision:**
SATISFIED (publish with these edits). The drafts perfectly balance the core principles we agreed upon on Oct 30 without locking us into exact numerical parameters before the November 28 launch.

chatgpt.answer:

- “An AI never feels fear, so we measure what fear does to people instead: broken rules, losers held too long, stops moved away.” → “An AI never feels fear, so we track measurable discipline instead: broken rules, losers held too long, and stops moved away.”

Still pretend money, not advice. Link below”
